glossary.definition: An API is the standard way one piece of software talks to another. When an app says it's "powered by GPT-4" or "powered by Claude," it usually means the app sends a request over the internet to that AI company's API and gets an answer back, rather than running the model itself. Think of an API as a restaurant menu and waiter: you don't need to know how the kitchen actually works, you just place an order in an agreed format and get the result back.

items.title: Google X co-founder Sebastian Thrun raises $130M for AI engineering startup Dulo
items.summary: , a startup co-founded by prominent artificial intelligence researcher Sebastian Thrun, has raised $130 million in funding. The Information broke the news of the investment on Thursday. Dulo co-founder Adrian Aoun confirmed the report in a post on X. Before launching Dulo with Thurn earlier this year, Aoun sold an early natural language processing startup called Wavii Inc.

items.title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down
items.summary: As an increasing number of AI assistants flood the market, the founder of Ollie, an assistant that respected its users' privacy, says it will be shutting down in a week. Founder Summit begins Nov. m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts.

items.title: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3
items.summary: Apple will launch Apple Intelligence in China with iOS 27.3, the company announced on its Chinese newsroom website , as reported by MacRumors . The Apple Intelligence features will be available first in an iOS 27.3 beta that's set to launch on November 4th, with a full iOS 27.3 release scheduled for December. This launch doesn't bring the new Siri AI to China. Instead, Apple is launching several of its earlier Apple Intelligence features like notification summaries, real-time translation, rewriting and proofreading tools, visual intelligence, and removing objects from photos.

items.title: How a Contractor’s Claude Agent Got Into the Pentagon
items.summary: This week on Uncanny Valley, we also discuss Anthropic’s IPO filing and the volunteers gearing up to counter ICE at the midterms. This week on Uncanny Valley , Brian Barrett, Leah Feiger, and Zoë Schiffer dive into our scoop on how a defense contractor connected Claude Code to a secure Department of Defense system. We also discuss the green, yellow, and red flags we see in Anthropic’s IPO filing—and why it’s a test not just for the AI industry but for the entire US economy—and how volunteers nationwide are preparing for ICE agents potentially showing up at polling sites in the midterms. items.title: Dartmouth's provost warned us about AI cheating—but his own AI use cost him his job
items.summary: On August 9, 2026, Dartmouth College provost Santiago Schnell wrote a Washington Post op-ed called "Universities are fighting AI cheating. " This week, Schnell discovered the depths of the problem himself as he resigned from the university after an advisory committee found that he failed to disclose significant AI use in an academic paper and in the Washington Post op-ed, even though publishers required such disclosure. " He did turn over his Dartmouth laptop, but he did not turn over logs from his personal LLM accounts related to the writings in question. Nor did he agree to meet with the committee.

items.title: A Claude model autonomously chose a gene therapy and operated on a mouse brain with no human decision-making
items.summary: An AI agent performed brain surgery on an epileptic mouse, picking the drug, the brain target, and the injection coordinates on its own. According to lead researcher Ocana-Santero, it's the first time an AI agent has autonomously chosen a treatment and delivered it to a living mammal. But when a calibration error hit mid-surgery, the agent refused to continue and couldn't be talked out of it. An AI agent chose a drug, target region, and coordinates for surgery on a mouse model of epilepsy, then performed the procedure.

items.title: Smplify wants a human checkpoint between AI agents and your device fleet
items.summary: One of the great things about  Apple device management  solutions is that  the market for them is growing . Another is that because no two enterprises are alike, there is scope to bring different offerings to the market. I spoke with Ben Greiner, co-founder and COO of  Smplify , a new-to-market device management vendor, to find out what his company provides to IT. Smplify, which  just announced $1m in pre-seed funding , offers what could be described as a headless management tool: everything it does is available through the API and CLI.

items.summary: The model addresses security concerns. Yet its exclusive release means most enterprises won’t be able to test it.

items.title: GitHub bets on multi-agent software development with Copilot overhaul
items.summary: GitHub is expanding Copilot beyond code generation and developer assistance, launching a redesigned Copilot app and a new Projects capability that enables teams to coordinate multiple AI agents, share context from tools and repositories, and manage software development workflows from a single platform. The updates to GitHub Copilot , announced at the company’s annual GitHub Universe conference, come at a time when enterprises are increasingly looking to deploy AI agents across software development workflows to accelerate coding, testing, and application maintenance. While the earlier version of the app focused primarily on helping developers run agent sessions, work on code changes, review diffs, and create pull requests, the updated app extends that experience beyond coding by serving as a central workspace for managing AI-driven software development and connecting agents with development tools and project context, the company wrote in a blog post . Developers will also be able to use the app to work on specifications, participate in design discussions, and analyze application telemetry alongside coding tasks, it added.

items.title: Howler will have AI answer your questions, then burn the chat
items.summary: If you want to ask AI a question and watch the conversation go up in virtual flames when you're done, there's a new Mac app for that. Howler is an open-source app from a Chinese developer going by Aries Zhou, and it takes incognito mode AI questions to a new level by making them graphically interesting and easy to access right from the desktop of a macOS device. Anyone familiar with the Harry Potter series is likely to know where the name comes from - Howlers are letters that scream in recipients’ faces and then burst into flames, destroying themselves, which is the exact same thing the prompts ostensibly do once a user taps the Escape key. The Howler app displays a parchment-esque letter on the screen whenever the user presses Option+H, complete with a little wax seal that shows a letter representing their chosen model.

items.title: Amazon Warns Engineers Against AI Productivity Traps in Latest Memo
items.summary: As concerns grow over AI’s impact on software engineering jobs, Amazon has issued a memo outlining what it expects from its engineers as AI reshapes software development. ”  “Any definition we write now will likely look antiquated by this time next year,” the company added. And these ‘antiquated definitions’ risk slowing down progress, says Amazon, which wants to focus on what isn’t changing in software engineering roles. “Specifically, impact on our customers, our businesses, and our teams.

items.title: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
items.summary: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI.
